```{r}
cordata <- dataset[, c("Fcare", "Fencourage","Fcontrol", "Mcare", "Mencourage", "Mcontrol", "Emotional abuse", "Physical abuse", "Sexual abuse", "Emotional neglect", "Physical neglect", "Pcoping", "Ncoping") ]


colnames(cordata) <- c("Care (Father)", "Encouragement (Father)", "Control (Father)",
                       "Care (Mother)", "Encouragement (Mother)", "Control (Mother)",
                       "Emotional abuse", "Physical abuse", "Sexual abuse",
                       "Emotional neglect", "Physical neglect",
                       "Positive coping", "Negative coping")

```

```{r}
cormatrix <- cor(cordata)
cormatrix
corrplot(cormatrix, method = "circle", type = "upper", tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45)
```

```{r}
cell_cor_p <- cor.mtest(cormatrix, conf.level = 0.95)$p
```

```{r}
par(family = "Times")
corrplot(cormatrix, 
         method = 'square',
         order = "hclust", 
         hclust.method='ward.D',
         type = "upper", 
         col = rev(brewer.pal(n=8, name="RdYlBu")),
         tl.cex=0.8,
         tl.col = "black",
         cl.cex = 0.5,
         cl.pos = "b",
         cl.length = 5,
         cl.ratio=0.1,
         p.mat = cell_cor_p,
         sig.level = 0.05,
         insig='label_sig',
         pch = '*',
         pch.col='red',
         pch.cex=1,
         mar=c(0, 0, 0, 0)) 
```

```{r}
# Load necessary library
library(ggplot2)

# Create data frame
data <- data.frame(
  Group = c(rep("Secure-adjusted", 30), rep("Ambivalent-strained", 30), rep("Disorganised-adversity", 30)),
  Positive_Coping_Mean = c(18.30, 15.09, 14.78),
  Positive_Coping_SE = c(0.32, 0.34, 0.97),
  Negative_Coping_Mean = c(11.13, 11.50, 13.98),
  Negative_Coping_SE = c(0.20, 0.23, 0.58)
)

# Simulate data for positive coping based on the mean and SE for each group
set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility
n <- 30  # Number of simulated data points per group

# Simulate positive coping data
data$Positive_Coping <- c(
  rnorm(n, mean = data$Positive_Coping_Mean[1], sd = data$Positive_Coping_SE[1]),
  rnorm(n, mean = data$Positive_Coping_Mean[2], sd = data$Positive_Coping_SE[2]),
  rnorm(n, mean = data$Positive_Coping_Mean[3], sd = data$Positive_Coping_SE[3])
)

# Simulate negative coping data
data$Negative_Coping <- c(
  rnorm(n, mean = data$Negative_Coping_Mean[1], sd = data$Negative_Coping_SE[1]),
  rnorm(n, mean = data$Negative_Coping_Mean[2], sd = data$Negative_Coping_SE[2]),
  rnorm(n, mean = data$Negative_Coping_Mean[3], sd = data$Negative_Coping_SE[3])
)

# Create the box plots for positive coping
ggplot(data, aes(x = Group, y = Positive_Coping)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of Positive Coping by Group", y = "Positive Coping")

# Create the box plots for negative coping
ggplot(data, aes(x = Group, y = Negative_Coping)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of Negative Coping by Group", y = "Negative Coping")

 

```

```{r}
# Load necessary library
library(ggplot2)

# Create data frame (same as before)
data <- data.frame(
  Group = c(rep("Secure-adjusted", 30), rep("Ambivalent-strained", 30), rep("Disorganised-adversity", 30)),
  Positive_Coping_Mean = c(18.30, 15.09, 14.78),
  Positive_Coping_SE = c(0.32, 0.34, 0.97),
  Negative_Coping_Mean = c(11.13, 11.50, 13.98),
  Negative_Coping_SE = c(0.20, 0.23, 0.58)
)
data
```


```{r}
# Simulate data for positive and negative coping (same as before)
set.seed(123)
n <- 30  # Number of simulated data points per group

# Simulate positive coping data
data$Positive_Coping <- c(
  rnorm(n, mean = data$Positive_Coping_Mean[1], sd = data$Positive_Coping_SE[1]),
  rnorm(n, mean = data$Positive_Coping_Mean[2], sd = data$Positive_Coping_SE[2]),
  rnorm(n, mean = data$Positive_Coping_Mean[3], sd = data$Positive_Coping_SE[3])
)

# Simulate negative coping data
data$Negative_Coping <- c(
  rnorm(n, mean = data$Negative_Coping_Mean[1], sd = data$Negative_Coping_SE[1]),
  rnorm(n, mean = data$Negative_Coping_Mean[2], sd = data$Negative_Coping_SE[2]),
  rnorm(n, mean = data$Negative_Coping_Mean[3], sd = data$Negative_Coping_SE[3])
)

# Create the enhanced box plot for Positive Coping
ggplot(data, aes(x = Group, y = Positive_Coping, fill = Group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 3, outlier.colour = "red", width = 0.7, alpha = 0.6) +  # Adjust boxplot appearance
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, size = 2, aes(color = Group), alpha = 0.6) +  # Add jittered points
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#66c2a5", "#fc8d62", "#8da0cb")) +  # Custom colors for groups
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#66c2a5", "#fc8d62", "#8da0cb")) +  # Match jitter color
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +  # Use minimal theme
  labs(title = "Boxplot of Positive Coping by Group", 
       y = "Positive Coping", x = "Group") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))  # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability

# Create the enhanced box plot for Negative Coping
ggplot(data, aes(x = Group, y = Negative_Coping, fill = Group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 3, outlier.colour = "red", width = 0.7, alpha = 0.6) +  # Adjust boxplot appearance
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, size = 2, aes(color = Group), alpha = 0.6) +  # Add jittered points
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#66c2a5", "#fc8d62", "#8da0cb")) +  # Custom colors for groups
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#66c2a5", "#fc8d62", "#8da0cb")) +  # Match jitter color
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +  # Use minimal theme
  labs(title = "Boxplot of Negative Coping by Group", 
       y = "Negative Coping", x = "Group") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))  # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability

```
